doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

title: Oddball ABC bumper recording session in New York
summary: Ricker and Jeff Tyzik played horns on a commercial bumper while the client gave vague requests such as a convertible feeling.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Indeed. Some of the odd — you mentioned putting strings — in your book — putting strings on a car commercial or something like that. I wonder if you have any memories of not necessarily terrible gigs but just oddball assignments that you might have taken on, working with producers or radio people, ad men, those kinds of things, and the odd things that they would ask for?

All I can think of is one I remember, it was around Thanksgiving a long time ago and it was on the Friday, the day after Thanksgiving. And myself and Jeff Tyzik and a couple of other guys had to go down to New York at this real fancy place, fancy recording studio. I can’t remember the name of it now but I know they were paying a lot of money for it.

And they were making a bumper, a little five second bumper that was going to be on ABC, you know, just a short little [scats] something like that. But out of that they were also writing a, they were going to take this bumper out of a longer piece. And so the rhythm section had already been done, okay? The tracks were there and we were the horns. And man we got going and this lady had her 12-year-old son there too and she started asking him things. I finally got the one thing from her, “I just want the feeling that I’m in my car in the convertible and I’m just driving a country road and the wind’s in my hair and it’s just a beautiful day.” And we’re banging our heads against — does that mean softer or louder? But we couldn’t translate what was going on, even — it was ridiculous. One thing she said, she said, “Do you have a cello?” You know like do you see a cello in here? No. It was crazy.
Meanwhile the clock is running, right?
It was running for them, yeah, and for us you know. I mean we got paid well but they just didn’t know.
